Done. The export succeeded on the first execution.

**What I built:** `out/T3/solution.py`, a plain torch plus safetensors script. It loads the input, casts the 64 projection matrices to bfloat16 via an anchored regex on the four exact module names, upcasts everything else to float32, drops the 48 attention buffers via a second anchored regex, and greedily packs tensors in sorted key order into shards under 256 MiB. The two embedding matrices exceed the budget and land alone in their own shards.

**Checks enforced before writing:** 244 input tensors, exactly 48 buffers dropped, exactly 64 bfloat16 tensors, layer-0 qkv is bfloat16, both embeddings are float32, 196 output tensors, shapes unchanged. After writing, the script reloads every shard and verifies bit-exact equality against the in-memory result and that the index maps all 196 names.

**Output:** 9 shard files named in the HuggingFace style plus `model.safetensors.index.json` in `out/T3/`. Shards 1 and 2 hold the embeddings alone. The remaining seven stay under the budget.

**Self-report:** written to `out/T3/REPORT.md`. Executions: 1, no failures. The one open ambiguity I noted is that the task does not specify tensor ordering or shard naming, so the hidden reference may differ on file names even though the sharding rules hold.
